edges.description: At high antibody titer, receptor blockade impairs downstream insulin signaling, driving extreme insulin resistance and hyperglycemia.

nodes.description: Loss of B-cell tolerance in a predisposed, frequently autoimmune host leads to production of polyclonal IgG autoantibodies directed against the insulin receptor. This humoral autoimmunity is the primary lesion of the syndrome and is the target of immunomodulatory therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Type B insulin resistance syndrome coexisting with aplastic anemia responsive to early immunosuppressive therapy.
evidence.snippet: Type B insulin resistance syndrome (IRS) is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by severe insulin resistance caused by autoantibodies against the insulin receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of type B insulin resistance: a novel approach to reduce insulin receptor autoantibodies.
evidence.snippet: Type B insulin resistance belongs to a class of diseases caused by an autoantibody to a cell surface receptor.

nodes.description: The NIH combination protocol of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, and pulse corticosteroids is aimed at suppressing pathogenic anti-insulin-receptor autoantibody production and has induced durable remission in treated patients.
nodes.id: Combination Immunomodulatory Therapy (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Pulse Corticosteroids)

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of type B insulin resistance: a novel approach to reduce insulin receptor autoantibodies.
evidence.snippet: This report focuses on seven patients who were treated with an intensive combination protocol of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, and pulse corticosteroids aimed at control of pathogenic autoantibody production.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of type B insulin resistance: a novel approach to reduce insulin receptor autoantibodies.
evidence.snippet: All seven treated patients achieved remission, defined as amelioration of hyperglycemia, discontinuation of insulin therapy, and resolution of hyperandrogenism.

nodes.description: Antibody-mediated blockade of the insulin receptor impairs the downstream insulin receptor signaling pathway in insulin target tissues (liver, muscle, adipose), producing extreme insulin resistance, refractory hyperglycemia, compensatory hyperinsulinemia, hypercatabolism/weight loss, acanthosis nigricans, and hyperandrogenism in women.
nodes.id: Impaired Insulin Signaling and Extreme Insulin Resistance

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of type B insulin resistance: a novel approach to reduce insulin receptor autoantibodies.
evidence.snippet: Blockade of insulin action results in hyperglycemia, hypercatabolism, severe acanthosis nigricans, and hyperandrogenism in women.
refractory transient hyperglycemia and extreme insulin resistance are the cardinal features, but hypoglycemia may also occur

nodes.description: The autoantibodies bind the insulin receptor and behave as partial agonists. At high titer they predominantly block insulin binding/signaling, producing severe insulin resistance; at low titer they can stimulate the receptor, producing hypoglycemia. This titer-dependent partial agonism explains the hallmark bimodal glycemic course.
nodes.id: Insulin Receptor Blockade and Partial Agonism

evidence.reference_title: Type B insulin resistance with glycemic extremes: a case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: These antibodies act as partial agonists, resulting in severe insulin resistance and hyperglycemia at high titer, and hypoglycemia at low titer.
